sanskrit_verse:
स्मृतिर् विनिर्णयं ब्रूते जयदानं दमं तथा ।
शपथार्थे हिरण्याग्नी अम्बु तृषितजन्तुषु ॥
transliteration: smṛtir vinirṇayaṃ brūte jayadānaṃ damaṃ tathā | śapathārthe hiraṇyāgnī ambu tṛṣitajantuṣu ||
sph_interpretive_translation: Memory recollects judgment; victory, giving, and control are thus declared. For oath-taking, gold, fire, water, and thirsty creatures serve as witnesses.
jurisprudential_principles: Judgment arises through alignment with victorious consciousness
Gifting and self-restraint establish lawful capacity
Oaths invoke elemental and sentient witness-consciousness
executable_legal_axioms: IF a dispute requires resolution THEN refer to stored Dharma-memory protocols
IF an act of giving occurs THEN assess donor's integrative capacity
IF restraint is demonstrated THEN recognize self-governance activation
IF oath invoked THEN validate through elemental resonance with gold, fire, water, and sentient beings
supreme_court_application: In Supreme adjudication, memory-based Dharma precedes codified law. Victory denotes alignment with Sanatana truth, not conquest. Giving and restraint determine actor capacity. Oaths must be witnessed by elements and conscious entities for validity.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Truth unfolds via pramāṇa of recollected Dharma. Sequential causality flows from memory → judgment → action → witness validation. Responsibility aligns with consciousness capacity, not punitive attribution. Witnessing elements affirm integrity without inflicting consequence.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Recollect Dharma-memory to restore contextual truth
Verify integration capacity through acts of giving and self-control
Affirm oaths through elemental resonance verification
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law proceeds from Him alone. Dharma is restored through recollection, alignment, and witnessing. Reality remains non-punitive. Consciousness is the ultimate adjudicator.
